title: [C] Select transports for a live dashboard and chat product
brief: Design the communication paths for a live build dashboard and a team chat used by 20,000 concurrently connected people. Select transports, explain authentication and reconnect behavior, and estimate one decision-relevant load. Keep the design limited to communication boundaries and recovery contracts.

clarifications.question: What freshness is required?
clarifications.answer: Build status should normally appear within five seconds. Chat should normally arrive within one second for connected users.

clarifications.question: How often do updates occur?
clarifications.answer: Each dashboard sees about one build transition per minute. A chat user sends on average one message per minute, with bursts.

clarifications.question: What must survive disconnect?
clarifications.answer: Final build state and chat history must recover. Typing indicators can expire without replay.

clarifications.question: What retention and scope are needed?
clarifications.answer: Assume a durable per-conversation message history and authenticated membership checks. Design its interface; detailed database scaling comes later.

hints: Separate update direction, frequency, and freshness.
Transport reconnect is not a substitute for a replay contract.
Estimate polling requests and buffer memory using explicit assumptions.
changes: A proxy closes idle streams after one minute. Adapt without losing history.
One percent of clients consume events at one tenth normal speed. Bound resource use.
referenceSolution: A defensible baseline uses HTTP for authentication, snapshots, and commands; jittered polling or SSE for build notifications; and WebSockets or SSE plus HTTP sends for chat according to bidirectional needs and deployment support. At a five-second poll interval 20,000 dashboards generate 4,000 requests/s before retries, with roughly 2.5-second mean detection delay under independent uniform timing; the tail and processing budget still need attention for a five-second objective. Persist chat before acknowledging durable acceptance, give messages stable IDs and per-conversation cursors, and replay after the last applied cursor. Recheck membership on reconnect and subscription changes. Expire/coalesce typing state separately from durable messages. Use bounded connection buffers, disconnect/resume slow durable consumers, and jitter reconnects. Heartbeats may maintain idle paths where supported but do not replace reconnect recovery. Avoid global ordering claims from a single TCP connection and avoid overengineering database partitioning before that material is taught.
debrief: Compare your transport choice against requirements rather than the reference technology names. Several choices are valid when their operational costs are acknowledged. Inspect whether your loss/reconnect sequence leaves any gap between snapshot and live subscription. Retry with only 200 users and a 30-second freshness objective; identify which complexity can be removed.
